rounds.text: DCG Cables & Wires Ltd is fundamentally mispriced at a modest P/E ratio of 11 [E1] and a price-to-book value of just 1.09x on a book value of ₹ 48.4 per share [E2] despite commanding a market capitalisation of ₹ 95.6 Cr [E3]. This valuation overlooks phenomenal top-line expansion, evidenced by a massive 62% compounded sales growth rate over five years [E8]. Furthermore, the business has successfully structurally expanded its profitability, driving operating margins up by 8 percentage points to 15% in March 2026 compared to 7% three years prior [E18]. This margin expansion underpins a respectable ROCE of 13.4% and an ROE of 10.4% [E6, E7]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4], the stock rests lowly at 18% of its 52-week range [E5], and quarterly operating margins compressed by 5 percentage points to 12% in March 2026 compared to the previous year [E19].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 11 and a price-to-book ratio of 1.09x on a book value of ₹ 48.4 per share with a market capitalisation of ₹ 95.6 Cr [E1, E2, E3], and compounded sales growth reached 62% over 5 years [E8]. However, this top-line expansion has failed to protect the stock price, which sits depressed at just 18% of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, while the bull celebrates long-term margin improvement, quarterly operating margin actually contracted by 5 percentage points down to 12% in March 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E19]. This recent margin compression directly threatens the sustainability of the reported 15% operating margin [E18]. Finally, the returns on capital—ROCE of 13.4% and ROE of 10.4% [E6, E7]—are modest at best, while the dividend yield of 0.00% [E4] offers investors no cash return while they wait for the stock to recover from near the bottom of its yearly range [E5].

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 1.09x (price ₹ 52.6 on a book value of ₹ 48.4).
The stock sits 18% of the way up its 52-week range (47 low to 79 high).
Compounded sales growth over 5 years is 62%.
Operating margin is 15% in Mar 2026 against 7% three years earlier (+8 percentage points).
Quarterly operating margin is 12% in Mar 2026 against 17% in the year-ago quarter (-5 percentage points).
